name: Jaw expansion via MSE / SARPE

lead: SARPE and MSE are ways to widen the upper jaw in adults. SARPE uses surgery to free the palate; MSE uses mini-implants to anchor an expander.
They are established orthodontic treatments for transverse deficiency, and forums discuss them for appearance.

paras: An expander applies force across the midpalatal suture, after surgical release in SARPE or via bone anchors in MSE/MARPE [1].
Reported problems include pain, relapse, periodontal effects and rare life-threatening haemorrhage [1][4][7].

lead: SARPE (surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion) and MSE (miniscrew-assisted or maxillary skeletal expander) are ways of widening the upper jaw in adults whose palatal suture has fused. Looksmaxxing communities discuss them for facial width and bite, often alongside braces or bimaxillary surgery.

In SARPE a surgeon cuts the midpalatal suture and an expander is then activated by an orthodontist [1]. MARPE anchors the expander with mini-implants for skeletal expansion without surgery, though most adult men may still need a surgical assist [1]. A literature review described SARPE as having gradually gained popularity for adults with maxillary transverse deficiency [2].
Studies describe complications and some relapse; haemorrhage has been reported in rare cases [3][4].
infobox: Oral and maxillofacial surgeon with orthodontist

paras: Rapid palatal expansion widens the upper jaw so teeth meet properly; it is most common at ages 8 to 18, and later treatment mostly tips teeth rather than widening bone [1]. For mature palates SARPE or MARPE is used [1][5].

A retrospective cohort at one US medical centre and a systematic review of complications examined adverse events after SARPE [6][7]. A report of 376 SARPE and 750 Le Fort I procedures documented life-threatening haemorrhage [4]. Wikipedia lists speech problems, pain, tongue sores, diastema and periodontal effects [1].
Studies have examined skeletal and dental changes and long-term stability, and compared SARPE with segmental Le Fort I osteotomy [8][9][10][11].

Published studies include case series of 14 adults [8], reviews [2][7] and a MARPE paper [5]. Registered trials compare 2- versus 3-segment SARPE (n=50) [12], tooth-borne, bone-borne and hybrid distraction (n=90) [13] and skeletal anchored expansion (n=90) [14].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org users compare SARPE and MSE and combine them with braces and jaw surgery, discussing expansion amounts and effects on cheek hollows [15][16][17].

claims.claim: SARPE can expand more than MSE, around 15 mm versus 12 mm.
Palatal expansion can change midface width and hollow cheeks.

timeline.event: Westcott and Angell pioneer early palatal expansion (1859 and 1860) [1].
